series.name: World of Outlaws
series.intro: Founded in 1978 by Ted Johnson, the World of Outlaws turned winged 410 sprint car racing into a national touring series, running coast to coast nearly every weekend from February to November.

legends.name: Steve Kinser
synopsis: Steve Kinser built the World of Outlaws into a national institution as much as any promoter did. Arriving for the series' first season in 1978, the Bloomington, Indiana, driver and his cousin Karl Kinser's team set the standard every touring sprint car program has chased since, and the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame later named him sprint car racing's greatest driver of the century.
He won the inaugural 1978 Outlaws title and 20 series championships in all. His 690 World of Outlaws A-feature wins are nearly 300 more than anyone else, a margin unmatched in American motorsports.

Kinser owned the sport's crown jewels. He won the Knoxville Nationals a record 12 times and the Kings Royal at Eldora seven times, the National Open at Williams Grove four times (1990, 1992, 1994 and 2003), and among the majors he won the Gold Cup Race of Champions at Chico more than ten times.
His 1987 season remains the benchmark. He won 46 Outlaws features that year, including 24 of the final 26.
Kinser was versatile beyond the dirt. He won the 1994 IROC race at Talladega, started the 1995 Daytona 500 and drove in the 1997 Indianapolis 500.

He briefly left the Outlaws for the National Sprint Tour in 2006, returned in 2007, and retired from sprint car racing in 2016. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2005 and the Motorsports Hall of Fame of America in 2017. His son Kraig, himself a 2005 Knoxville Nationals winner, carried the family name forward.
achievements: 690 World of Outlaws feature wins (all-time record)
legends.snippet: Steve Kinser is the winningest driver in World of Outlaws history, with 20 WoO championships and 690 feature wins. "The King" won the inaugural 1978 Outlaws title, a record 12 Knoxville Nationals and seven Kings Royals.
stats: Crown jewels: 12 Knoxville Nationals, 7 Kings Royals, 4 National Opens
legends.photo_caption: Steve Kinser at Knoxville Raceway, Aug. 11, 2004.

legends.name: Sammy Swindell
synopsis: Sammy Swindell was the engineer of the modern sprint car as much as its driver. A technically minded Tennessean from a racing family, he was one of the Memphis-area group that helped make the early World of Outlaws, and alongside Steve Kinser and Doug Wolfgang he is remembered as one of the "Big Three" of winged sprint car racing.

He won Outlaws championships in 1981 and 1982. In 1997 he won a third title in his own car, becoming the first owner-driver to win the WoO crown. He was also runner-up four times, and his 394 World of Outlaws A-main wins rank second all-time.
Swindell won the 1983 Knoxville Nationals and the Kings Royal in 1992, 1999 and 2012. In 1981 he took the wing off to win the Pacific Coast Nationals at Ascot.
In midgets he won the Chili Bowl five times: 1989, 1992, 1996, 1998 and 2009.

Swindell also tested himself elsewhere. He made CART starts in 1985 and 1986, failed to qualify for the 1987 Indianapolis 500, and ran the inaugural 1995 NASCAR Truck Series season, finishing 12th in points.
He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2006.
legends.snippet: Sammy Swindell is a three-time World of Outlaws champion (1981, 1982, 1997) whose 394 WoO feature wins rank second all-time. He also won the 1983 Knoxville Nationals, three Kings Royals and five Chili Bowl Midget Nationals, and in 1997 he became the first owner-driver to win the Outlaws title.
stats: Crown jewels: 1 Knoxville Nationals, 3 Kings Royals, 2 National Opens
legends.photo_caption: Sammy Swindell at Knoxville Raceway, August 1997.

legends.name: Donny Schatz
synopsis: Donny Schatz built the most sustained championship program of the World of Outlaws' modern era. The Fargo, North Dakota, driver was the series' 1997 Rookie of the Year, won his first Outlaws feature in 1998, and joined Tony Stewart's team in 2008. That partnership with Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing ran 18 seasons and produced most of his titles.
Schatz won ten World of Outlaws championships: 2006 through 2009, 2012, and 2014 through 2018. Only Steve Kinser has won more. He has more than 300 Outlaws feature wins, which rank third all-time.
He won the Knoxville Nationals 11 times, in 2006–09, 2011–15, 2017 and 2022, one short of Kinser's record. He also won six Kings Royals and a record six National Opens at Williams Grove.
Fans know him for his consistency across a full season and his command of sprint car racing's crown-jewel events.
achievements: 6 Kings Royal and 6 National Open wins
2 Grand Annual Sprintcar Classic wins at Warrnambool, Australia (2001, 2002)
legends.snippet: Donny Schatz is a ten-time World of Outlaws champion, second only to Steve Kinser, and an 11-time Knoxville Nationals winner. Driving for Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing from 2008, he also won six Kings Royals and a record six Williams Grove National Opens.
stats: Crown jewels: 11 Knoxville Nationals, 6 Kings Royals, 6 National Opens, 2 Australian Classics
legends.photo_caption: Donny Schatz in his Tony Stewart Racing firesuit, 2025 World of Outlaws portrait.

legends.name: Mark Kinser
synopsis: Mark Kinser of Oolitic, Indiana, is a cousin of Steve Kinser. He was World of Outlaws co-Rookie of the Year in 1984 and ran his own team for a decade before joining his father, Karl Kinser, in 1995.
He won World of Outlaws championships in 1996 and 1999 and was runner-up in 1991, 1998 and 2001. His 203 World of Outlaws wins rank fourth all-time.
He won the Knoxville Nationals in 1996, 1999 and 2000 and the 2001 Kings Royal at Eldora. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2014.
legends.snippet: Mark Kinser won World of Outlaws titles in 1996 and 1999, and his 203 series wins rank fourth all-time. He also won the Knoxville Nationals three times.
achievements: National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (2014)
legends.photo_caption: Mark Kinser's No. 5 Mopar sprint car at Knoxville Raceway, Aug. 13, 1999.

legends.name: Doug Wolfgang
synopsis: Doug Wolfgang carried the Midwest's homegrown sprint car scene onto the national stage. The Sioux Falls, South Dakota, driver came up in super modifieds and, with car owner Bob Trostle, broke through at Knoxville in the mid-1970s before becoming one of the "Big Three" of the early World of Outlaws era.
Wolfgang won the Knoxville Nationals five times, in 1977, 1978, 1984, 1985 and 1989. He won them for four different owners: Trostle, Bill Smith, Bob Weikert and Danny Peace.
With the Outlaws he finished second in the standings four times and won 140 features, fifth-most in series history. He also won 37 All Star Circuit of Champions races and two Kings Royals.

On April 3, 1992, a fiery crash at Lakeside Speedway in Kansas City left him with burns over about 30 percent of his body and a broken vertebra. He came back to win an IMCA 360 sprint championship and the 1996 ASCS 360 Nationals, then retired in 1997 after another serious crash.
Wolfgang is a member of the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame and later built sprint car chassis from his shop near Sioux Falls.
achievements: 37 All Star Circuit of Champions wins
3 straight Williams Grove National Open wins (1984, 1985, 1986) for Bob Weikert
legends.snippet: Doug Wolfgang of Sioux Falls, South Dakota, is a five-time Knoxville Nationals champion with 140 World of Outlaws feature wins, fifth-most all-time. He was one of the "Big Three" of the early Outlaws era, and he also won two Kings Royals and 37 All Star Circuit of Champions races.
stats: Crown jewels: 5 Knoxville Nationals, 2 Kings Royals, 3 National Opens
legends.photo_credit: World of Outlaws photo (photographer not identified)
legends.photo_caption: Doug Wolfgang's sprint car at a World of Outlaws race in Lawrenceburg, Ind.

series.name: High Limit Racing
series.intro: Brad Sweet and Kyle Larson launched High Limit Racing in 2022, and it became a full touring series in 2023. Interstate Batteries is now its title sponsor. The series is young, but it has already become a major stage for wing sprint car racing.

legends.name: Rico Abreu
synopsis: Rico Abreu has been part of High Limit Racing from its start and helped build it into a national tour. Abreu is a Northern Californian who has achondroplasia and is four feet four inches tall. He has run every High Limit points race since 2023 and holds the series' career records for wins, starts, podiums and top-10 finishes.
He made his name in midgets. He won the 2014 USAC National Midget championship, then won the Chili Bowl Midget Nationals in back-to-back years, 2015 and 2016.

Stock cars came next, with backing from his friend Kyle Larson. He won the 2015 NASCAR K&N Pro Series East race at Columbus Motor Speedway, his first stock car win, before returning to open-wheel racing.

Back on dirt, he became a regular winner at marquee events, including the Outlaws and High Limit shows at Eldora's 4-Crown. He won his first national sprint car championship, the 2025 High Limit title, by winning the season finale at Texas Motor Speedway. He retained the High Limit championship in 2026 with Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing, winning eight High Limit features that season.
legends.snippet: Rico Abreu won consecutive High Limit Racing championships in 2025 and 2026, with eight High Limit wins in 2026. He is the series' all-time leader in wins, starts, podiums and top-10 finishes. He also won the 2014 USAC National Midget championship and back-to-back Chili Bowl Midget Nationals in 2015 and 2016.
legends.photo_caption: Rico Abreu, World of Outlaws.

legends.name: Kyle Larson
legends.snippet: Kyle Larson co-founded High Limit Racing, won its first championship and put together the 2020 dirt season people still measure everything against: 46 wins in 97 starts. He is a three-time NASCAR Cup Series champion (2021, 2025 and 2026), a 2015 Rolex 24 at Daytona winner, and a winner of the Coca-Cola 600 and the Brickyard 400.
synopsis: Kyle Larson of Elk Grove, California, came up through California micros and midgets before NASCAR came calling. He never left dirt behind.

In 2020, with NASCAR on hold for him, he raced dirt almost every night and won 46 of 97 starts in sprint cars, midgets, Silver Crown and a dirt late model. That is a .474 winning percentage against the best drivers in the sport. Running only 26 of the 54 World of Outlaws events, he still led the series with 12 wins. He also won his first Chili Bowl that year, swept Indiana Midget Week, and won the Hoosier Hundred and the Bettenhausen 100 on the dirt miles.

With Brad Sweet he announced High Limit Racing at Eldora in July 2022. He won the series' inaugural championship in 2023, and in late 2023 High Limit took over the All Star Circuit of Champions from Tony Stewart. Through the 2026 national season he had 15 High Limit wins.

His dirt crown jewels include three Chili Bowls (2020, 2021, 2025), three Knoxville Nationals (2021, 2023, 2024) and the 2021 Kings Royal. In NASCAR he won the Cup Series championship with Hendrick Motorsports in 2021, with 10 wins, again in 2025, and a third time in 2026 at Homestead-Miami Speedway, becoming a back-to-back champion. He also won the 2021 Coca-Cola 600 and the 2024 Brickyard 400, and in sports cars he won the 2015 Rolex 24 at Daytona with Jamie McMurray and Chip Ganassi Racing. He was named one of NASCAR's 75 Greatest Drivers.
achievements: 2020: 46 wins in 97 dirt starts; 12 World of Outlaws wins, most in the series
2015 Rolex 24 at Daytona winner (with Jamie McMurray, Chip Ganassi Racing)
legends.photo_caption: Kyle Larson in Casey's Victory Lane at the Knoxville Nationals, 2025.

series.name: All Star Circuit of Champions
series.intro: Bud Miller founded the All Star Circuit of Champions in 1970 as a touring 410 winged sprint car series built around Ohio. Bert Emick revived it in 1980 and ran it through 2002, Tony Stewart bought it in 2015, and High Limit Racing acquired it after the 2023 season. It sat out 2024 and returned in 2025 with Ohio Sprint Speedweek still at its heart.

legends.name: Dale Blaney
synopsis: Dale Blaney is the winningest driver in All Star Circuit of Champions history, with 137 feature wins. The Hartford, Ohio, driver won six series titles, in 1995, 1996, 2008, 2013, 2014 and 2015, tying the series record.
His title runs span two decades. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2016.
achievements: 2016 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame
legends.photo_caption: Dale Blaney in the car built by his brother Dave Blaney at Sharon Speedway, World of Outlaws.

legends.name: Kenny Jacobs
synopsis: Kenny Jacobs of Holmesville, Ohio, ranks second all-time in All Stars feature wins with 97. He won four straight All Star Circuit of Champions titles, from 1998 through 2001.
He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2007.
achievements: 2007 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame
legends.photo_caption: Kenny Jacobs' No. 71M sprint car, St. Augustine, Fla., Feb. 12, 1994.

legends.name: Chad Kemenah
synopsis: Chad Kemenah of Findlay, Ohio, won six All Star Circuit of Champions titles, tying Dale Blaney's series record. He won four straight from 2002 through 2005, then added back-to-back crowns in 2016 and 2017.
His championships span 16 seasons. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2023.
achievements: 2023 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame
legends.photo_caption: Chad Kemenah at Volusia, Feb. 8, 2006 (All Stars).

legends.name: Tim Shaffer
synopsis: Tim Shaffer of Aliquippa, Pennsylvania, the Steel City Outlaw, won four straight All Star Circuit of Champions titles, from 2009 through 2012. His 69 All Stars feature wins rank fourth all-time.
He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2020.
achievements: 2020 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame

legends.name: Frankie Kerr
synopsis: Frankie Kerr won four All Star Circuit of Champions titles in the 1990s, in 1991, 1993, 1994 and 1997, and 52 All Stars features.
He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2016.
achievements: 2016 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame

legends.name: Joey Saldana
synopsis: Joey Saldana, the Brownsburg Bullet, ranks third all-time in All Stars feature wins with 74. In 1995 he set the series single-season record with 18 wins in the Art Wendt No. 77w.
He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2023.
He won the Kings Royal at Eldora Speedway in 2002 and again in 2006.
achievements: Series record 18 wins in a season (1995)
2023 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame
legends.photo_credit: World of Outlaws photo (photographer not identified)
legends.photo_caption: Joey Saldana, World of Outlaws.

legends.name: Jack Hewitt
synopsis: Jack Hewitt of Troy, Ohio, was the people's hero of Midwestern dirt racing. He was a racer's racer who would run anything, anywhere, and he was the son of racer Don Hewitt. He was a fan favorite as much for his personality as his driving. Blunt and outspoken, he never minced words, and fans loved him for it.

He won the 1985 All Star Circuit of Champions title with 12 wins that year, and his 55 All Stars feature wins rank fifth all-time. He also won 46 USAC National Sprint Car features and Silver Crown titles in 1986 and 1987.

In 1998 he reached the Indianapolis 500 and finished 12th. That same year he swept all four features at Eldora's 4-Crown Nationals, in Silver Crown, Sprint, Midget and modified, for four different teams. In all he has won 19 4-Crown features, the most of anyone.
He is a member of the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (2002) and the USAC Hall of Fame.
achievements: National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (2002)
1985 All Star Circuit of Champions champion
Only driver to sweep all four features at Eldora's 4-Crown Nationals (1998)
legends.snippet: Jack Hewitt of Troy, Ohio, won the 1985 All Star Circuit of Champions title and ranks fifth all-time in All Stars feature wins. Blunt and outspoken, he never minced words, and that made him one of the biggest fan favorites in Midwestern dirt racing.
legends.photo_caption: Jack Hewitt in a USAC sprint car at Winchester, April 2, 1995.

series.name: USAC Sprint Cars
series.intro: USAC's National Sprint Car championship dates to 1956. It is non-winged 410 racing, and it has long been a proving ground for drivers headed to Indianapolis and NASCAR.

legends.name: Pancho Carter
synopsis: Pancho Carter set the template for USAC versatility. The son of USAC Hall of Famer Duane Carter, he became the organization's first career Triple Crown champion and showed a generation of short-track drivers that one racer could master midgets, sprints and Silver Crown cars.

He won the 1972 USAC National Midget title and Sprint Car titles in 1974 and 1976. In 1978 he won the Silver Crown title, then called the USAC National Dirt Championship. He scored 70 USAC national feature wins across those series.
Carter was the 1974 Indianapolis 500 Rookie of the Year and made 17 Indy 500 starts. He won the pole in 1985 and finished third in 1982. He also won the 1981 Michigan 500.
He is a member of both the National Sprint Car and National Midget Halls of Fame and the USAC Hall of Fame.
legends.snippet: Pancho Carter was USAC's first career Triple Crown champion. He won the 1972 National Midget title, the 1974 and 1976 Sprint Car titles and the 1978 Silver Crown title. He also made 17 Indianapolis 500 starts, won the 1985 Indy pole and won the 1981 Michigan 500.
legends.photo_caption: Pancho Carter, USAC.

legends.name: Dave Darland
synopsis: Dave Darland was USAC's everyman champion. Fans called him the "People's Champ." Over nearly four decades he made more USAC national starts than anyone, 1,334, and he showed that a local Indiana sprint car racer could become one of the sport's all-time greats.
Born in 1966 in Lincoln, Indiana, he won four national titles: Silver Crown in 1997, Sprint in 1999, and Midget in 2001 and 2002. That made him the third career Triple Crown champion.

His 62 USAC National Sprint Car wins were the record when he retired in 2023. His 20 Indiana Sprint Week wins are still the most of any driver. He won 115 USAC features nationally and regionally, including 30 National Midget and 14 Silver Crown wins.
He won at least one USAC national feature in a record 24 straight seasons, 1993 through 2016. Along the way he won Turkey Night, the midget classic, twice.
Darland is a member of the USAC Hall of Fame.
legends.snippet: Dave Darland, the "People's Champ," is a USAC Triple Crown champion with titles in Silver Crown (1997), Sprint (1999) and Midget (2001–02). He retired in 2023 with 62 USAC National Sprint Car wins, then the record, and a record 20 Indiana Sprint Week wins.
legends.photo_caption: Dave Darland, USAC.

legends.name: Brady Bacon
synopsis: Brady Bacon of Broken Arrow, Oklahoma, won USAC National Sprint Car championships in 2014, 2016, 2020 and 2021.

Through the 2026 season he had 64 USAC National Sprint Car wins, second all-time. He has won at least one series feature in every season since 2011, a USAC Sprint record of 16 consecutive seasons, and he and the Dynamics, Inc. team rank among the winningest driver and owner pairings in series history.
legends.snippet: Brady Bacon won four USAC National Sprint Car titles, and his 64 series wins through 2026 rank second all-time.
achievements: 64 USAC National Sprint Car wins through 2026 (2nd all-time)
Record streak of 16 consecutive seasons with a USAC Sprint win, dating to 2011
legends.photo_caption: Brady Bacon in victory lane after winning round five of USAC Indiana Sprint Week at Circle City Raceway (July 28, 2026).

legends.name: Tom Bigelow
synopsis: Tom Bigelow, a Wisconsin native who made his home in Winchester, Indiana, won the 1978 USAC National Sprint Car championship.

His 52 USAC National Sprint Car wins stood as the series record from 1981 until Dave Darland passed him in 2014, and they still rank fourth all-time. He also ranks first in series history in fast-qualifier awards.
He is a member of the USAC Hall of Fame (2013), the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame and the National Midget Auto Racing Hall of Fame.
legends.snippet: Tom Bigelow was the 1978 USAC National Sprint Car champion, and his 52 series wins were the all-time record for more than 30 years.
achievements: 52 USAC National Sprint Car wins (4th all-time)
USAC Sprint win record holder, 1981 to 2014
USAC, National Sprint Car and National Midget Halls of Fame
legends.photo_caption: Tom Bigelow, USAC.

legends.name: Tracy Hines
synopsis: Tracy Hines spent most of a quarter-century as a full-time competitor in all three USAC national divisions. He was the son of a New Castle, Indiana, midget racing family, and his father Jim and brother Ted were champions too. He later helped build other drivers' programs as a team executive.
He broke through in 1996, winning his first National Midget race at Winchester in his first start back from a fiery crash.
Hines won the Silver Crown title in 2000 and the Sprint title in 2002. In 2015, after announcing his retirement midseason, he won the Midget title and completed the Triple Crown.
He scored 91 USAC national wins, including 47 in sprint cars, 35 in midgets and nine in Silver Crown. He won at least one national feature in 19 straight seasons, 1996 through 2014.
Away from USAC he raced in NASCAR's Truck and Busch series.
legends.snippet: Tracy Hines is a USAC Triple Crown champion with Silver Crown (2000), Sprint (2002) and Midget (2015) titles. He won 91 USAC national races, including 47 in sprint cars, and he won at least one national feature in 19 straight seasons.
legends.photo_caption: Tracy Hines, USAC.

legends.name: Justin Grant
synopsis: Justin Grant of Ione, California, built his record on durability. In July 2025 he set the record for consecutive USAC National Sprint starts, with 325, and he became the series' all-time wins leader.

Grant was the 2010 USAC National Sprint Rookie of the Year. He won Silver Crown titles in 2020 and 2025 and National Sprint titles in 2022 and 2023. He has also won the National Drivers championship five times.

In September 2025 at Lucas Oil Speedway he won his 63rd National Sprint feature, breaking Dave Darland's record, and that season he became the eighth driver with 100 USAC wins. He finished the 2026 season with 71 USAC National Sprint Car victories, his sixth and final 2026 win coming Aug. 29 at Kokomo.
achievements: USAC National Sprint all-time wins leader
2022 and 2023 USAC National Sprint Car champion
71 USAC National Sprint Car wins through 2026
legends.snippet: Justin Grant is the all-time wins leader in USAC National Sprint Car racing, finishing the 2026 season with 71 series victories. He was the 2022 and 2023 USAC National Sprint Car champion, won Silver Crown titles in 2020 and 2025, and has won the USAC National Drivers championship five times.
legends.photo_caption: Justin Grant, 2025 Mike Curb USAC National Drivers Champion.

legends.name: Jack Hewitt
synopsis: Jack Hewitt of Troy, Ohio, was the people's hero of Midwestern dirt racing. He was a racer's racer who would run anything, anywhere, and he was the son of racer Don Hewitt. He was a fan favorite as much for his personality as his driving. Blunt and outspoken, he never minced words, and fans loved him for it.

He won 46 USAC National Sprint Car features, plus Silver Crown titles in 1986 and 1987 and the 1985 All Star Circuit of Champions title. His 23 Silver Crown wins rank second all-time, and he also won seven USAC Midget races.

In 1998 he reached the Indianapolis 500 and finished 12th. That same year he swept all four features at Eldora's 4-Crown Nationals, in Silver Crown, Sprint, Midget and modified, for four different teams. In all he has won 19 4-Crown features, the most of anyone.
He is a member of the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (2002) and the USAC Hall of Fame.
achievements: National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (2002)
1985 All Star Circuit of Champions champion
Only driver to sweep all four features at Eldora's 4-Crown Nationals (1998)
legends.snippet: Jack Hewitt of Troy, Ohio, won 46 USAC National Sprint Car features and swept all four features at Eldora's 4-Crown Nationals in 1998. Blunt and outspoken, he never minced words, and that made him one of the biggest fan favorites in Midwestern dirt racing.
legends.photo_caption: Jack Hewitt in a USAC sprint car at Winchester, April 2, 1995.

series.name: Northern Auto Racing Club (NARC)
series.intro: Founded in 1960, the Northern Auto Racing Club is Northern California's home for 410 sprint cars. In 2017 the King of the West series was rebranded under the NARC name.

legends.name: Brent Kaeding
synopsis: Brent Kaeding of Campbell, California, is the second of three generations of Northern California open-wheel champions. His father, Howard, raced modifieds and super modifieds, and his son Tim and nephew Bud also became top 410 sprint car drivers. Brent won his first NARC race at Silver Dollar Speedway in Chico in April 1981 and went on to win a record 13 NARC championships, including eight in a row.

Over a career of more than three decades he won hundreds of features, an estimated 375 to more than 400, and he holds career win records at tracks from Chico to Tulare. He also won 13 Golden State Challenge titles and four Trophy Cup championships, and he won the 1985 Turkey Night Grand Prix at Ascot.
legends.snippet: Brent Kaeding of Campbell, California, won a record 13 Northern Auto Racing Club (NARC) 410 sprint car championships, including eight in a row. He also won 13 Golden State Challenge titles, four Trophy Cups and the 1985 Turkey Night Grand Prix.

series.name: National Championship Racing Association (NCRA)
series.intro: The NCRA ran a 410 winged Outlaw sprint car tour across the central Great Plains from 1988 to 2004, along with a 360 division. Gary Wright, profiled in the ASCS section, won the 410 tour nine years running.

legends.name: Gary Wright
synopsis: Gary Wright owned the NCRA 410 tour in the 1990s. The Texan won nine consecutive NCRA championships from 1993 through 2001 and more than 75 series features, taking over the series from his longtime friend and traveling companion Terry Gray.

Wright then carried that dominance into the American Sprint Car Series, where he became the winningest driver in series history with 128 National Tour feature wins between 1994 and 2011 and four straight National Tour titles from 2004 through 2007. He also won with the All Star Circuit of Champions and the World of Outlaws, and his total career feature wins top 400. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2011.
achievements: 2011 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame
legends.snippet: Gary Wright won nine consecutive NCRA 410 sprint car championships from 1993 through 2001 and more than 75 NCRA features. The Texan later became the winningest driver in ASCS history with 128 National Tour wins and was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2011.
legends.photo_credit: ASCS / World Racing Group (photographer not identified)
legends.photo_caption: Gary Wright, ASCS.

legends.name: Terry Gray
synopsis: Terry Gray was the first star of the NCRA 410 tour. By the time the series launched, the Bartlett, Tennessee, privateer had been racing since 1974 and had a World of Outlaws feature win at Riverside Speedway in Arkansas from 1980 on his record, and he had won with USA as well. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2022.

On the NCRA 410 tour, Gray led the series in wins in its first two seasons and won NCRA championships in 1989, 1990 and 1992 before his longtime friend and traveling companion Gary Wright began his run of titles. He then took that experience into ASCS, where he won four straight titles from 1995 through 1998, and into USCS, where he won 16 championships.
achievements: He earned his 99th career USCS feature victory at Dixie Speedway on September 5, 2026.
2022 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame
legends.snippet: Terry Gray won NCRA 410 sprint car championships in 1989, 1990 and 1992 and led the series in wins in its first two seasons. The Bartlett, Tennessee, driver later won four ASCS and 16 USCS titles and entered the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2022.
legends.photo_credit: ASCS / World Racing Group (photographer not identified)
legends.photo_caption: Terry Gray, ASCS.

series.name: American Sprint Car Series (ASCS)
series.intro: Emmett Hahn founded the American Sprint Car Series in 1993. Its National Tour became the leading national stage for 360 winged sprint cars, racing across Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas and the wider Midwest and South.

legends.name: Gary Wright
synopsis: Gary Wright is the winningest driver in American Sprint Car Series history, with 128 National Tour feature wins between 1994 and 2011. He won four consecutive ASCS National Tour championships, from 2004 through 2007.

Before his ASCS peak, Wright dominated the NCRA 410 tour. He won nine consecutive NCRA championships from 1993 through 2001 and more than 75 series features. He also won with the All Star Circuit of Champions and the World of Outlaws, and his total career feature wins top 400. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2011.
achievements: 2011 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame
legends.snippet: Gary Wright is the winningest driver in American Sprint Car Series (ASCS) history, with 128 National Tour wins and four straight titles from 2004 to 2007. He also won nine consecutive NCRA championships and was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2011.
legends.photo_credit: ASCS / World Racing Group (photographer not identified)
legends.photo_caption: Gary Wright, ASCS.

legends.name: Terry Gray
synopsis: Terry Gray was one of the first drivers to sign up for the American Sprint Car Series, and by the mid-1990s he was the driver it measured itself against. The Bartlett, Tennessee, privateer, who owned and maintained his own cars, had been racing since 1974 and scored his first major win in a World of Outlaws feature at Riverside Speedway in Arkansas in 1980. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2022.

In 1995 Gray won the ASCS National Tour championship, and he won it again in each of the next three seasons. Those four straight titles from 1995 through 1998 came with 43 wins and stood as the series record for 22 years. He later became the cornerstone of the United Sprint Car Series.
achievements: He earned his 99th career USCS feature victory at Dixie Speedway on September 5, 2026.
2022 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame
legends.snippet: Terry Gray of Bartlett, Tennessee, won four straight American Sprint Car Series (ASCS) National Tour championships from 1995 through 1998. The 2022 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame inductee also won 16 USCS titles and three NCRA championships.
legends.photo_credit: ASCS / World Racing Group (photographer not identified)
legends.photo_caption: Terry Gray, ASCS.

legends.name: Sam Hafertepe Jr.
synopsis: Sam Hafertepe Jr. of Sunnyvale, Texas, won his first ASCS National Tour feature at I-30 Speedway in 2010. He became the series' dominant driver of the modern era and won five consecutive National Tour championships from 2016 through 2020, breaking Terry Gray's record of four in a row.

He ranks second on the National Tour's all-time wins list behind Gary Wright, whom he has called the driver everyone wanted to be like when he started. Through the 2026 season he had 95 ASCS National Tour feature wins, including seven in 2026, and seven National Tour championships, the most in series history.
achievements: 7 ASCS National Tour championships through 2026 (series record)
95 ASCS National Tour feature wins through 2026, including seven in 2026
2nd on ASCS National Tour all-time wins list
legends.snippet: Sam Hafertepe Jr. won seven American Sprint Car Series (ASCS) National Tour championships through 2026, the series record, including five straight titles from 2016 to 2020. He has 95 ASCS National Tour feature wins through 2026, including seven in 2026, and ranks second on the National Tour's all-time wins list.
legends.photo_caption: Sam Hafertepe Jr.'s No. 15 sprint car, World of Outlaws (2021 story).

legends.name: Jason Johnson
synopsis: Jason Johnson of Eunice, Louisiana, was a 360 sprint car great on the ASCS National Tour. He won series titles in 2008, 2010, 2012, 2013 and 2014, and he and his wife, Bobbi, also won ASCS owner titles with Jason Johnson Racing.

He moved to the World of Outlaws in 2015 and was the series Rookie of the Year. In 2016 he outdueled Donny Schatz to win the Knoxville Nationals, a win fans and historians remember as one of the biggest upsets in the event's history, second only to Bobby Allen's in 1990. He won 12 World of Outlaws features, the only Louisiana native to win in the series.
He died in 2018 and was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2019.
legends.snippet: Jason Johnson, "The Ragin' Cajun," won five ASCS National Tour titles, then beat Donny Schatz for the 2016 Knoxville Nationals, one of the biggest upsets in the event's history.
achievements: 2015 World of Outlaws Rookie of the Year
National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (2019)

series.name: United Sprint Car Series (USCS)
series.intro: Pete Walton's Atlanta-based United Sprint Car Series has raced 360 winged sprint cars on dirt and asphalt across the Southeast since the late 1990s.

legends.name: Terry Gray
synopsis: No driver is more closely tied to the United Sprint Car Series than Terry Gray. The Bartlett, Tennessee, veteran, who began racing in 1974, has been the series' cornerstone for more than two decades, racing as a privateer who builds and maintains his own equipment. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2022.

Gray has raced the United Sprint Car Series regularly since 2001 and has missed only a handful of its events. He won the 2024 Outlaw Thunder Tour title, his 16th USCS national championship. He earned his 99th career USCS feature victory at Dixie Speedway on September 5, 2026. He also fields cars as an owner in the series.
achievements: He earned his 99th career USCS feature victory at Dixie Speedway on September 5, 2026.
2022 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame
legends.snippet: Terry Gray is the defining driver of the United Sprint Car Series (USCS), with 16 national championships. He earned his 99th career USCS feature victory at Dixie Speedway on September 5, 2026. The Bartlett, Tennessee, privateer also won four ASCS titles and was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2022.
legends.photo_credit: ASCS / World Racing Group (photographer not identified)
legends.photo_caption: Terry Gray, ASCS.

series.name: USAC Midgets
series.intro: Midgets are small, light open-wheel cars with powerful engines. USAC's National Midget championship began in 1956, and its alumni include many drivers who went on to race at Indianapolis and in NASCAR.

legends.name: Mel Kenyon
synopsis: Mel Kenyon and his brother Don built a family midget operation that set the standard in USAC National Midget racing. Don was his car owner and crew chief, and they also built their own chassis. From 2004 to 2009 their Kenyon Midget Series ran under USAC sanction.

Mel won 111 USAC National Midget races, the series record. He won seven national championships over 21 years: 1964, 1967, 1968, 1974, 1977, 1981 and 1985. He also won at least one race in 21 straight seasons, 1962 through 1982.

Most of that came after a fiery 1965 champ car crash at Langhorne that burned off the fingers of his left hand. The brothers designed a special glove that fit over a stud on the steering wheel so he could steer with his palm.
Kenyon made eight Indianapolis 500 starts and finished in the top five in half of them, with a best of third in 1968.
He retired in 2009 after more than 50 years of midget racing and 925 USAC National Midget starts.
legends.snippet: Mel Kenyon, the "King of the Midgets," holds the USAC National Midget record with 111 feature wins and seven championships between 1964 and 1985. He won those races after losing the fingers of his left hand in a 1965 crash, and he made eight Indianapolis 500 starts.
legends.photo_caption: Mel Kenyon, USAC.

legends.name: Rich Vogler
synopsis: "Rapid Rich" Vogler of Glen Ellyn, Illinois, the son of midget winner Don Vogler, was the most prolific winner of USAC's short-track era. In 1980 he became the first driver to win the USAC Sprint and Midget championships in the same year.

He won five National Midget titles, in 1978, 1980, 1983, 1986 and 1988, and Sprint titles in 1980 and 1989. His 134 USAC national wins break down to 95 Midget, 35 Sprint and four Silver Crown. Only A.J. Foyt has more.
Vogler won the Hut Hundred eight times and the 4-Crown midget race four times. He also won the inaugural Chili Bowl in 1987, and his 16 wins in 100-lap midget races are the most of anyone.
He made five Indianapolis 500 starts, with a best of eighth in 1989.

Vogler was killed on July 21, 1990, while leading a sprint car race at Salem Speedway, five days before his 40th birthday. Under USAC rules the race reverted to the last completed lap, so he was declared the winner of the last race he started.
legends.snippet: Rich Vogler won five USAC National Midget championships and the 1980 and 1989 USAC Sprint Car titles. His 95 National Midget wins rank second all-time, and he won the inaugural 1987 Chili Bowl and the Hut Hundred eight times.
legends.photo_caption: Rich Vogler, USAC.

legends.name: Bob Wente
synopsis: Bob Wente was a pillar of USAC midget racing's formative years, and he raised a family that kept racing midgets. All three of his sons competed in USAC Midget racing.
He began racing midgets in 1954. He was runner-up in the national standings three years in a row before winning the 1963 USAC National Midget championship.
Wente won 78 National Midget races, third all-time behind Mel Kenyon and Rich Vogler. He won the 1963 Hut Hundred and the Night Before the 500 in 1969 and 1976.
In his only Indianapolis 500, in 1964, he started 32nd and finished ninth.
He was in the inaugural class of the National Midget Auto Racing Hall of Fame in 1984. He died in 2000.
achievements: Inaugural National Midget Hall of Fame class (1984)
legends.snippet: Bob Wente was the 1963 USAC National Midget champion, and his 78 National Midget wins rank third all-time. He won the Hut Hundred and two Night Before the 500 races, finished ninth in the 1964 Indianapolis 500 and was in the inaugural Midget Hall of Fame class.
legends.photo_caption: Bob Wente, USAC.

legends.name: Dave Darland
synopsis: Dave Darland was best known for sprint cars, but he also won the USAC National Midget championship in 2001 and 2002 and earned 30 National Midget wins. His midget titles were part of what made him a USAC career Triple Crown champion.
For his full career, including his sprint and Silver Crown titles, see his USAC Sprint entry.
legends.snippet: Dave Darland won the USAC National Midget championship in 2001 and 2002 and earned 30 National Midget wins. Those titles helped make him a USAC Triple Crown champion alongside his Sprint and Silver Crown crowns.
legends.photo_caption: Dave Darland, USAC.

series.name: USAC Silver Crown
series.intro: The Silver Crown series traces back to the old USAC Championship dirt races. Since 1971 it has been its own championship for big, front-engine Champ Dirt Cars on dirt and pavement ovals, and it is the closest link to the roadsters of early Indianapolis.

legends.name: Kody Swanson
synopsis: Kody Swanson of Kingsburg, California, has defined USAC Silver Crown racing for more than a decade. He set records in the series that may never be approached.

He won the 2005 Western Sprint title and the 2009 Silver Crown Rookie of the Year award. He won his first Silver Crown title in 2014, and his eight titles (2014, 2015, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022 and 2024) are the most any driver has won in a single USAC national series.
His 49 Silver Crown wins and 59 poles are both series records by a wide margin. He won his eighth title in 2024 despite racing through an injury.
He also won the 2017 Jason Leffler Award.
On pavement, Swanson has won the Little 500 at Anderson Speedway four times, in 2016, 2018, 2019 and 2026, tying Tom Cherry for third on the event's all-time wins list.
legends.snippet: Kody Swanson holds the USAC Silver Crown records for championships, with eight, and wins, with 49. Those eight titles are the most any driver has won in a single USAC national series, and he also holds the series record of 59 poles, and he has won the Little 500 at Anderson Speedway four times (2016, 2018, 2019 and 2026).
legends.photo_caption: Kody Swanson, 2024 USAC Silver Crown National Champion.

legends.name: Jack Hewitt
synopsis: Jack Hewitt of Troy, Ohio, was the people's hero of Midwestern dirt racing. He was a racer's racer who would run anything, anywhere, and he was the son of racer Don Hewitt. He was a fan favorite as much for his personality as his driving. Blunt and outspoken, he never minced words, and fans loved him for it.
He won Silver Crown titles in 1986 and 1987 and the 1985 All Star Circuit of Champions title. His 23 Silver Crown wins rank second all-time. He also won 46 USAC Sprint and seven Midget races.

In 1998 he reached the Indianapolis 500 and finished 12th. That same year he swept all four features at Eldora's 4-Crown Nationals, in Silver Crown, Sprint, Midget and modified, for four different teams. In all he has won 19 4-Crown features, the most of anyone.
He is a member of the USAC Hall of Fame.
achievements: All Star Circuit of Champions champion
Won the 1991 Grand Annual Sprintcar Classic at Warrnambool, Australia
legends.snippet: Jack Hewitt of Troy, Ohio, was the 1986 and 1987 USAC Silver Crown champion, and his 23 Silver Crown wins rank second all-time. In 1998 he swept all four features at Eldora's 4-Crown Nationals and raced in the Indianapolis 500.
legends.photo_caption: Jack Hewitt in a USAC sprint car at Winchester, April 2, 1995.

legends.name: Dave Steele
synopsis: Dave Steele of Tampa, Florida, may have been the greatest pavement racer in USAC history. All 60 of his USAC national wins, from 1996 to 2007, came on asphalt.
He moved to the Midwest for the 1996 season. In his first USAC National Sprint start, at Lakeside Speedway, he swept the night: fastest qualifier, heat win and feature win.
Steele won 16 Silver Crown, 26 Sprint and 18 Midget races, even though he usually ran half the schedule or less. He ran the full Silver Crown schedule in 2004 and 2005 and won the title both years.
In 2002 he won two National Midget features in one night at Indianapolis Raceway Park, coming from 22nd in the second. He is a member of the USAC Hall of Fame.
legends.snippet: Dave Steele of Tampa, Florida, won back-to-back USAC Silver Crown championships in 2004 and 2005 and was perhaps USAC's greatest pavement racer. All 60 of his USAC national wins came on asphalt: 16 in Silver Crown, 26 in sprint cars and 18 in midgets.
legends.photo_caption: Dave Steele, USAC.

series.name: USAC Triple Crown
series.intro: The USAC Triple Crown goes to drivers who win national championships in all three USAC divisions: Midget, Sprint and Silver Crown. Only eight drivers have done it, listed here in the order they completed it. Tony Stewart (1995) and J.J. Yeley (2003) swept all three in a single season.

legends.name: Pancho Carter
synopsis: Pancho Carter set the template for USAC versatility. The son of USAC Hall of Famer Duane Carter, he became the organization's first career Triple Crown champion and showed a generation of short-track drivers that one racer could master midgets, sprints and Silver Crown cars.

He won the 1972 USAC National Midget title and Sprint Car titles in 1974 and 1976. In 1978 he won the Silver Crown title, then called the USAC National Dirt Championship. He scored 70 USAC national feature wins across those series.
Carter was the 1974 Indianapolis 500 Rookie of the Year and made 17 Indy 500 starts. He won the pole in 1985 and finished third in 1982. He also won the 1981 Michigan 500.
He is a member of both the National Sprint Car and National Midget Halls of Fame and the USAC Hall of Fame.
legends.snippet: Pancho Carter was USAC's first career Triple Crown champion. He won the 1972 National Midget title, the 1974 and 1976 Sprint Car titles and the 1978 Silver Crown title. He also made 17 Indianapolis 500 starts, won the 1985 Indy pole and won the 1981 Michigan 500.
legends.photo_caption: Pancho Carter, USAC.

legends.name: Tony Stewart
synopsis: The Columbus, Indiana, driver won the 1994 USAC National Midget title. In 1995 he won the Midget, Sprint and Silver Crown championships, the first driver ever to sweep all three in a single season. He won 27 USAC National Midget races, 10 Sprint races and three Silver Crown races.

Stewart won the 1997 Indy Racing League title and started on the pole for the 1996 Indianapolis 500. He then won three NASCAR Cup championships as a driver, in 2002, 2005 and 2011, the last as an owner-driver for Stewart-Haas Racing. He is the only driver to win championships in both IndyCar and NASCAR. He also won the Brickyard 400 in 2005 and 2007, the Chili Bowl Midget Nationals in 2002 and 2007, and the 2006 IROC championship.

As a car owner, his record is separate from those driving titles. Tony Stewart Racing won nine World of Outlaws Sprint Car owner championships: the first with Danny Lasoski in 2001, in the team's inaugural season after Stewart formed TSR in November 2000, and eight more with Donny Schatz in 2008, 2009, 2012 and 2014 through 2018. Schatz joined TSR for the 2008 season after winning the 2006 and 2007 Outlaws titles with his own Donny Schatz Motorsports team. He and TSR parted ways on August 12, 2025, during a winless season; Kerry Madsen finished 2025 in the No. 15. TSR has not won another World of Outlaws title since Schatz's last one in 2018 (Brad Sweet won the series in 2020 and 2022). In 2026, after that split, Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing won the High Limit Racing owner title with Rico Abreu, Abreu's second straight High Limit driving championship and Stewart's first as a High Limit owner; Abreu's 2025 High Limit title was with his own team.

Official USAC entrant-champion records credit Stewart with seven National Sprint Car owner titles and seven Silver Crown owner titles. The Sprint titles were with J.J. Yeley (2003), Josh Wise (2006) and Levi Jones (2007, 2009, 2010 and 2011), and Bryan Clauson (2013). The Silver Crown titles were with Yeley (2002 and 2003) and Dave Steele (2004 and 2005) under East-Stewart Racing, co-owned with Bob East, then with Jones (2010 and 2011) and Bobby East (2013) under Tony Stewart Racing / Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing. Two often-cited years are not official Stewart owner titles: Jay Drake won the 2004 Sprint driver championship in a TSR car, but the USAC Sprint entrant title that year went to Dynamics, Inc. #69; Bobby East won the 2012 Silver Crown driver championship in a TSR car, but the official entrant title that year went to RW Motorsports/Curb-Agajanian Racing #17.

Stewart-Haas Racing added NASCAR Cup owner championships in 2011, with Stewart driving, and in 2014 with Kevin Harvick. SHR also won two NASCAR Xfinity Series owner championships with Cole Custer in the No. 00: the 2018 owners title (Custer finished second in driver points to Tyler Reddick) and the 2023 title, when Custer also won the driver championship. SHR did not win a NASCAR Truck Series owner championship. In 2023 Matt Hagan won the NHRA Funny Car world championship for Tony Stewart Racing, the team's first NHRA title.

In 2024 Stewart drove the team's Top Fuel dragster himself, reached two final rounds, made the Countdown to the Championship and was named NHRA Rookie of the Year. He was inducted into the National Midget Hall of Fame in 2001, the USAC Hall of Fame in 2016, the Motorsports Hall of Fame of America in 2019, the NASCAR Hall of Fame in 2020 and the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2022.
achievements: Driver: 1995 single-season USAC Triple Crown (Midget, Sprint, Silver Crown); 1994 National Midget title
Driver: 1997 Indy Racing League champion; 1996 Indianapolis 500 pole
Driver: 3 NASCAR Cup titles (2002, 2005, 2011, the last as owner-driver)
Driver: Brickyard 400 wins in 2005 and 2007; Chili Bowl Nationals wins in 2002 and 2007; 2006 IROC champion
Owner: 9 World of Outlaws titles — Danny Lasoski (2001) and Donny Schatz (2008, 2009, 2012, 2014–18); Schatz joined TSR in 2008 and left Aug. 12, 2025
Owner: 2026 High Limit Racing title with Rico Abreu (Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing)
Owner: 7 USAC National Sprint titles — Yeley (2003), Wise (2006), Jones (2007, 2009–11), Clauson (2013)
Owner: 7 USAC Silver Crown titles — Yeley (2002–03) and Steele (2004–05) with East-Stewart Racing; Jones (2010–11) and Bobby East (2013)
Owner: 2 NASCAR Cup titles with Stewart-Haas Racing (2011 with Stewart, 2014 with Kevin Harvick)
Owner: 2 NASCAR Xfinity titles with Stewart-Haas Racing and Cole Custer (2018 owners championship; 2023 driver and owner title)
Owner: 2023 NHRA Funny Car world title with Matt Hagan
legends.snippet: Tony Stewart is the first driver to win all three USAC national championships in one season, sweeping the Midget, Sprint and Silver Crown titles in 1995. He won the 1997 IndyCar title and three NASCAR Cup championships (2002, 2005 and 2011). As a car owner he has nine World of Outlaws titles with Danny Lasoski and Donny Schatz, the 2026 High Limit title with Rico Abreu, seven USAC Sprint and seven Silver Crown owner championships, two NASCAR Cup and two Xfinity owner titles, and the 2023 NHRA Funny Car title.
stats: Owner: 7 USAC Sprint and 7 Silver Crown titles
Owner: 2 NASCAR Cup titles (2011 Stewart, 2014 Harvick)
legends.photo_caption: Tony Stewart, World of Outlaws.

legends.name: Dave Darland
synopsis: Dave Darland was USAC's everyman champion. Fans called him the "People's Champ." Over nearly four decades he made more USAC national starts than anyone, 1,334, and he showed that a local Indiana sprint car racer could become one of the sport's all-time greats.
Born in 1966 in Lincoln, Indiana, he won four national titles: Silver Crown in 1997, Sprint in 1999, and Midget in 2001 and 2002. That made him the third career Triple Crown champion.

His 62 USAC National Sprint Car wins were the record when he retired in 2023. His 20 Indiana Sprint Week wins are still the most of any driver. He won 115 USAC features nationally and regionally, including 30 National Midget and 14 Silver Crown wins.
He won at least one USAC national feature in a record 24 straight seasons, 1993 through 2016. Along the way he won Turkey Night, the midget classic, twice.
Darland is a member of the USAC Hall of Fame.
legends.snippet: Dave Darland, the "People's Champ," is a USAC Triple Crown champion with titles in Silver Crown (1997), Sprint (1999) and Midget (2001–02). He retired in 2023 with 62 USAC National Sprint Car wins, then the record, and a record 20 Indiana Sprint Week wins.
legends.photo_caption: Dave Darland, USAC.

legends.name: J.J. Yeley
synopsis: J.J. Yeley's 2003 season remains the high-water mark for a USAC driver. Racing Tony Stewart's sprint and Silver Crown cars and the Steve Lewis midget Stewart had driven in 1995, he won all three national championships and 24 USAC races. That broke the single-season record of 19 set by A.J. Foyt.
Yeley won Indiana Sprint Week and USAC Sprint Rookie of the Year in 1997. He finished ninth in the 1998 Indianapolis 500 despite a first-lap spin.

After an IndyCar run in 2000, he returned to USAC. He won the Sprint title in 2001, the Silver Crown title in 2002, and then the 2003 sweep, joining Stewart as the only drivers to win the Triple Crown in a single season.
He moved to NASCAR with Joe Gibbs Racing in 2004 and has raced in the national touring series ever since.
legends.snippet: J.J. Yeley swept all three USAC national championships in 2003, joining Tony Stewart as the only single-season Triple Crown winners. His 24 USAC wins that year broke A.J. Foyt's single-season record, and he also won the 2001 Sprint and 2002 Silver Crown titles.

legends.name: Jerry Coons Jr.
synopsis: Jerry Coons Jr. brought Arizona into USAC's elite. The Tucson driver made his National Midget debut in 1987 and has 430 series starts, among the most ever, and he became one of USAC's most respected veterans.
His first National Midget win came at the 1996 Belleville Midget Nationals. He later became the first three-time winner of that race, in 2005, 2007 and 2012.

Coons won the National Midget championship in 2006 and 2007. In 2008 he won both the Sprint and Silver Crown titles to complete the career Triple Crown. USAC named him National Midget Driver of the Decade for 2000–09.
At Eldora's 4-Crown Nationals he won in all three USAC divisions: Silver Crown in 2007 and 2014, Sprint in 2009 and Midget in 2010.
legends.snippet: Jerry Coons Jr. of Tucson, Arizona, is a USAC Triple Crown champion. He won the National Midget titles in 2006 and 2007, then both the Sprint and Silver Crown titles in 2008. He was USAC's Midget Driver of the Decade for 2000–09 and the first three-time winner of the Belleville Midget Nationals.
legends.photo_caption: Jerry Coons Jr., USAC.

legends.name: Tracy Hines
synopsis: Tracy Hines spent most of a quarter-century as a full-time competitor in all three USAC national divisions. He was the son of a New Castle, Indiana, midget racing family, and his father Jim and brother Ted were champions too. He later helped build other drivers' programs as a team executive.
He broke through in 1996, winning his first National Midget race at Winchester in his first start back from a fiery crash.
Hines won the Silver Crown title in 2000 and the Sprint title in 2002. In 2015, after announcing his retirement midseason, he won the Midget title and completed the Triple Crown.
He scored 91 USAC national wins, including 47 in sprint cars, 35 in midgets and nine in Silver Crown. He won at least one national feature in 19 straight seasons, 1996 through 2014.
Away from USAC he raced in NASCAR's Truck and Busch series.
legends.snippet: Tracy Hines is a USAC Triple Crown champion with Silver Crown (2000), Sprint (2002) and Midget (2015) titles. He won 91 USAC national races, including 47 in sprint cars, and he won at least one national feature in 19 straight seasons.
legends.photo_caption: Tracy Hines, USAC.

legends.name: Chris Windom
synopsis: Chris Windom of Canton, Illinois, showed how far a family-run program could go in USAC. He won the Little 500 in 2011 and again in 2015.
He won the Silver Crown title in 2016 and the National Sprint title in 2017. In 2020 he won the National Midget title and became the seventh career Triple Crown champion.
Windom won Indiana Sprint Week in 2011 and 2018, the Eastern Storm in 2017 and 2018.
He has also raced stock cars, including the 2021 NASCAR Cup race on the Bristol dirt, and in recent seasons he has moved toward winged sprint car racing.
legends.snippet: Chris Windom became USAC's seventh Triple Crown champion with the 2016 Silver Crown, 2017 National Sprint and 2020 National Midget titles. The Canton, Illinois, driver is also a two-time Little 500 and two-time Indiana Sprint Week winner.
legends.photo_caption: Chris Windom's NOS Energy Drink sprint car, 2025 World of Outlaws.

legends.name: Logan Seavey
synopsis: Logan Seavey of Sutter, California, and Abacus Racing built one of USAC's most complete modern programs. Abacus became only the second team to win owner titles in all three national divisions.
Seavey won the 2018 National Midget championship as a rookie.

In 2023 he won both the Silver Crown and National Midget titles. He added the 2024 Sprint title, along with Indiana Sprint Week and the National Drivers championship, to become the eighth career Triple Crown champion.
In 2023 he swept all three USAC features at Eldora's 4-Crown Nationals. In 2025 he won in all three divisions again, 11 times in all.
He won the Chili Bowl Midget Nationals in 2023 and again in 2024.
achievements: Chili Bowl Nationals winner in 2023 and 2024
legends.snippet: Logan Seavey became USAC's eighth Triple Crown champion when he added the 2024 National Sprint title to his 2023 Silver Crown and his 2018 and 2023 National Midget titles. He did it with Abacus Racing, which won owner titles in all three divisions.
legends.photo_caption: Logan Seavey, 2024 USAC AMSOIL Sprint Car National Champion.

series.name: Old School Legends
series.intro: Fan favorites and era icons who don't clear the DirtSprintCars Legend Standard on titles and series records, but still belong in any conversation about the greats.

legends.name: Kenny Weld
synopsis: Kenny Weld grew up in a Kansas City racing family. At 18 he won the 1964 Knoxville Nationals, and he won again in 1965, 1972 and 1973 to become the event's first four-time winner.

Driving the Weikert Livestock Special in Pennsylvania, he won 43 features in 1973 and a record fifth straight Williams Grove track title in 1974. He is credited with 189 feature wins between 1967 and 1975.
After driving he became a builder, from the dirt modified "Batmobile" to Weld Tech. He died in 1997, the year he entered the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame.
legends.snippet: Kenny Weld was the first four-time Knoxville Nationals winner and the man to beat in Pennsylvania in the early 1970s. He later made his mark as a builder.
achievements: Record five straight Williams Grove track titles
National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (1997)
legends.photo_credit: World of Outlaws archive photo (photographer not identified)
legends.photo_caption: Kenny Weld after his fifth straight track title, Williams Grove, Pa., Oct. 5, 1974.

legends.name: Jan Opperman
synopsis: Jan Opperman was one of the original outlaws. Discovered in California in 1968, he raced anywhere that paid, which kept him from piling up records with any one sanctioning body.

He won the 1971 Knoxville Nationals and the Western World Championship that same season, then won 44 features in 1972. In 1976 he won the Hulman Classic at Terre Haute. He also co-designed the Maxwell sprint car and made two Indianapolis 500 starts.

With long hair and a charisma few others had, he was one of the most beloved drivers in the sport and a big draw everywhere he raced. Crashes in 1976 and 1981 cut his career short. He was in the first class of the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 1990.
legends.snippet: Jan Opperman was one of the original outlaws, a long-haired racer who chased the best-paying shows across the country. He won the 1971 Knoxville Nationals and 44 features in 1972, and his charisma made him one of the most beloved drivers in the sport.
achievements: National Sprint Car Hall of Fame, inaugural class (1990)
legends.photo_credit: World of Outlaws photo (photographer not identified)
legends.photo_caption: Jan Opperman's Bogar No. 90 at a USAC race at Eldora Speedway, Ohio.

legends.name: Jac Haudenschild
synopsis: Jac Haudenschild of Wooster, Ohio, was the most fearless driver the World of Outlaws ever saw. Even from ninth or 10th he could amaze a crowd, and he never burned a bridge, driving for 14 different winning car owners in the series.

He won 72 World of Outlaws features, from the 1982 Eldora Nationals to his last series win at Eldora in 2010. His best points finish was second in 1995. He won the Kings Royal three times (1987, 1994, 1998), the Gold Cup three times and the 2003 Mopar Million.
He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2009 while still racing, and ran his final race at the 2021 World Finals.
legends.snippet: Jac Haudenschild, "The Wild Child," was the most fearless driver in World of Outlaws history. He won 72 series features and three Kings Royals, and fans never took their eyes off him.
achievements: National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (2009)
legends.photo_caption: Jac Haudenschild with his son Sheldon Haudenschild (cropped to Jac), World of Outlaws.

legends.name: Bobby Allen
synopsis: Bobby Allen grew up in Miami racing go-karts, then headed to Pennsylvania as a teenager because that was where the sprint cars ran three and four nights a week. He became one of the sport's original outlaws.

He was known for doing a lot with a little. He built his own chassis, put together his own engines and made his own setup calls on the familiar No. 1a, spending what money he had on the car rather than on how it looked.

On Aug. 18, 1990, in front of about 18,000 fans, his homebuilt car beat the well-funded Sammy Swindell to win the Knoxville Nationals. It is remembered as the biggest upset in the event's history. He won more than 275 sprint car features, including 30 with the World of Outlaws and 46 with the All Star Circuit of Champions, where he won the 1980 title.
He entered the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 1988 and later owned the Shark Racing team with his grandson Logan Schuchart. He died in 2025 at 81.
legends.snippet: Bobby Allen did a lot with a little. In 1990 the low-budget racer drove his homebuilt No. 1a past Sammy Swindell to win the Knoxville Nationals, still remembered as the biggest upset in the event's history.
achievements: 1980 All Star Circuit of Champions champion
National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (1988)
legends.photo_caption: Bobby Allen at Hagerstown, May 24, 1987, World of Outlaws.

legends.name: Brad Doty
synopsis: Brad Doty of Ohio was World of Outlaws and Knoxville Nationals Rookie of the Year in 1982. He won 18 World of Outlaws features and 73 sprint car features in all, and he finished second to Steve Kinser in the 1987 World of Outlaws standings.

A crash on the opening lap of the 1988 Kings Royal at Eldora left him paralyzed from the chest down. He never left the sport. He started the Brad Doty Classic in 1989 and from 1992 became the best-known television voice of winged sprint car racing.
He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2001.
legends.snippet: Brad Doty was a World of Outlaws winner and 1987 points runner-up whose driving career ended in the 1988 Kings Royal. He stayed in the sport as a promoter and its best-known TV analyst, and fans have never stopped loving him for it.
achievements: 1982 World of Outlaws Rookie of the Year
National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (2001)
legends.photo_caption: Brad Doty at Attica, July 14, 2020, World of Outlaws.

active_note: * Active driver, still racing as of 2026.
